item.title: The Maccabi Tel Aviv Row Could Bring Down a Police Chief
item.description: Confidence in the police chief lost after the Israeli fan ban Plus: With interest rates rising, does the UK student loan system need reform? ‘The Voice of Hind Rajab’ director discusses the true story that cannot be forgotten. With Michael Walker, Barry Malone, and Kaouther Ben Hania…

item.title: Palestine Action Prisoners End Hunger Strike
item.description: Palestine Action-linked remand prisoners have ended their hunger strike, claiming some of their key demands have been met. Harriet Williamson reports.

item.title: Today’s Public Intellectuals Are More Likely to Serve Power Than Challenge It | Juliet Jacques
item.description: 30 years ago, the BBC invited Palestinian thinker Edward Said to deliver six lectures on the public intellectual, writes Juliet Jacques. Can you imagine something so outlandish happening today?

item.title: NHS Trust Spent Millions on Controversial ‘Spy Camera’ Tech Despite Damning Internal Report
item.description: Exclusive: An NHS trust spent over £2.4m on Oxevision, a technology that films vulnerable patients in their bedrooms 24/7, even after its own internal evaluation report highlighted significant issues with the tech and the conduct of its parent company. Harriet Williamson reports.

item.title: Trump Backs Down Over Iran Strike
item.description: The US weighs its military options in Iran. Plus: Robert Jenrick sacked from the shadow cabinet, and the eyebrow-raising attempt at rewriting the history of October 7th. With NoJusticeMTG & Dalia Gebrial.…

item.title: How Many More Tory Defectors Can Reform Absorb? | Ash Sarkar
item.description: Reform claims to break with the broken Westminster model while lining its ranks with former ministers - something that might undermine Nigel Farage’s disruptor-in-chief charade, argues Ash Sarkar.

item.title: Jeremy Corbyn and Zarah Sultana Are on Rival Slates for Your Party Leadership
item.description: Exclusive: Jeremy Corbyn has announced his slate of candidates to contest Your Party’s inaugural central executive committee elections and decide the future direction and leadership of the new left party. Harriet Williamson reports.

item.title: This Billionaire Landlord Bullied Journalists Into Deleting Negative Coverage of Him
item.description: ‘Rogue landlord’ John Christodoulou owes hundreds of thousands of pounds to former tenants. Instead of paying them, he is pressuring journalists to remove coverage of his unlawful behaviour. Rivkah Brown reports.

item.title: The Proxy War in Your Party
item.description: Jeremy Corbyn and Zarah Sultana are putting up rival slates of candidates for elections to Your Party’s executive committee. Plus: The latest on ICE’s mass deportation campaign, an exclusive report into NHS spending on a controversial surveillance system that films vulnerable inpatients, and Donald Trump finally gets his Nobel Peace Prize - sort of. With Michael Walker, Steven Methven, Jennifer Forbes & Max Shanly.…

item.title: Exposing the Lies of the 20th Century | Aaron Bastani meets Tariq Ali.
